title: Arithmetic and geometric sequences and series

questions.question: In a theatre there are n rows of seats. The first row has a seats, and each later row has 4 more seats than the row before, so the seats per row form an arithmetic sequence (2nd row a + 4, 3rd row a + 8). The total number of seats in the first 10 rows is 360. Find the value of a.
steps: Arithmetic sequence with first term a and common difference d = 4.
Sum of first n terms: S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1)d].

questions.question: The first row of a theatre has 18 seats and each row has 4 more seats than the row before. The total number of seats in the n rows is 2146. Show that n^2 + 8n - 1073 = 0.

For the theatre with first row 18 seats and 4 more seats in each row, the total seats in n rows satisfies n^2 + 8n - 1073 = 0. (i) State the number of rows in the theatre. (ii) Find the maximum number of seats in any one row. (Marks shown for part (c) as a whole: 3.)
steps: The number of rows is positive, so n = 29.
The largest row is row 29: a_29 = 18 + 4(28) = 130 seats.

questions.question: A company extracted 480 tonnes of silver from a mine in year 1, 465 tonnes in year 2 and 450 tonnes in year 3, and so on, forming an arithmetic sequence. Find the mass of silver extracted in year 14.
steps: First term a = 480 and common difference d = 465 - 480 = -15.

questions.question: A silver mine has first-year extraction 480 tonnes and common difference -15 tonnes per year. After a total of 7770 tonnes has been extracted, the company stops mining at the end of year N. Show that N^2 - 65N + 1036 = 0.

The company stopped mining at the end of year N, after a total of 7770 tonnes was extracted, where the annual extraction falls by 15 tonnes each year from 480 tonnes. State the value of N, using N^2 - 65N + 1036 = 0.
questions.answer: N = 28 (N = 37 is rejected because annual extraction would be negative from year 34).
steps: Annual extraction is 480 - 15(n - 1), which is zero at year 33 and negative after that.
So N = 37 is not possible, and N = 28.

questions.question: Ben saves 100 pounds in the first month and, in each later month, 5 pounds more than the previous month (105 in month 2, 110 in month 3, and so on), forming an arithmetic sequence over 60 months. Find the amount Ben saves in the 40th month.
steps: First term a = 100, common difference d = 5.
So Ben saves 295 pounds in month 40.

questions.question: Ben saves 100 pounds in the first month and 5 pounds more each month than the month before, over a period of 60 months. Find the total amount Ben saves over the 60-month period.
steps: So the total saved is 14850 pounds.

questions.question: Lina saves 600 pounds in the first month and, in each later month, 10 pounds less than the previous month (590 in month 2, 580 in month 3, and so on), forming an arithmetic sequence. After n months she has saved exactly 18200 pounds. Form an equation in n and show that it can be written as n^2 - 121n + 3640 = 0.
Solve the equation n^2 - 121n + 3640 = 0 from part (c).
Lina saves 600 pounds in month 1 and 10 pounds less each month than the previous month. State, with a reason, which solution of n^2 - 121n + 3640 = 0 is not a sensible value for n.
questions.answer: n = 65 is not sensible: her monthly saving would be negative after month 61.
steps: Monthly saving in month n is 600 - 10(n - 1), which is 0 when n = 61.
For months after 61 the monthly amount is negative, which is not a sensible saving.
So n = 65 is not sensible, and n = 56 is valid.

questions.question: An arithmetic series has first term a and common difference d. Prove that the sum of the first n terms is (1/2) n [2a + (n - 1)d].
steps: Write the same sum in reverse: S_n = [a + (n - 1)d] + ... + (a + d) + a.
Add the two forms: each pair adds to 2a + (n - 1)d, and there are n pairs.

questions.question: A company making 200 mobile phones each week increases production by 20 each week (220 in week 2, 240 in week 3, and so on) until it is producing 600 in week N. Find the value of N.

A company makes 200 phones in week 1, increasing by 20 each week until it makes 600 in week 21, and then continues to make 600 each week. Find the total number of mobile phones made in the first 52 weeks, starting from and including week 1.
steps: Weeks 1 to 21 form an arithmetic series with a = 200, d = 20, n = 21.
Weeks 22 to 52 are 31 weeks at 600 phones each: 31 x 600 = 18600.

questions.question: An arithmetic series has first term alpha and common difference d. Prove that the sum to n terms of this series is (n/2){2alpha + (n - 1)d}.
steps: Write S_n again in reverse order and add the two forms.
Each pair sums to 2alpha + (n - 1)d, and there are n pairs.

questions.question: A sequence u_1, u_2, u_3, ... is given by u_n = 5n + 3(-1)^n. Find the value of u_5.
For the sequence u_n = 5n + 3(-1)^n, find the sum of u_n from n = 1 to 59.
steps: Split the sum: 5 times the sum of n plus 3 times the sum of (-1)^n.
Sum of 5n for n = 1 to 59 is 5 x 59 x 60/2 = 5 x 1770 = 8850.
Sum of (-1)^n for n = 1 to 59: the terms cancel in pairs from n = 1 to 58, leaving (-1)^59 = -1.

questions.question: A geometric sequence has first term a and common ratio r, where r > 0. The 3rd term is 20 and the 5th term is 12.8. Show that r = 0.8.
A geometric sequence has common ratio r = 0.8 and 3rd term 20. Find the value of a, the first term.

A geometric sequence has a = 31.25 and r = 0.8. The sum of the first n terms is greater than 156. Find the smallest possible value of n, using algebra (solutions based entirely on graphical or numerical methods are not acceptable).
Given that log_a b = k, find in simplest form in terms of k: log_a(sqrt(a)/b).
Given that log_a b = k, find in simplest form in terms of k: (log_a(a^2 b))/(log_a(b^3)).
steps: Numerator: log_a(a^2 b) = log_a(a^2) + log_a(b) = 2 + k.

questions.question: Given that log_a b = k, find in simplest form in terms of k: the sum from n = 1 to 50 of (k + log_a(b^n)).
steps: log_a(b^n) = n log_a(b) = nk, so each term is k + nk = k(n + 1).
Sum: k times the sum of (n + 1) for n = 1 to 50 = k(sum of n + 50).
Sum of n from 1 to 50 is 1275, so the total = k(1275 + 50) = 1325k.

questions.question: Kim's annual salary in year 1 is 16200 pounds and is predicted to be 31500 pounds in year 10. Model A assumes her salary increases by the same amount each year. According to model A, find Kim's annual salary in year 2.
steps: Model A is arithmetic with a = 16200 and u_10 = 31500.

questions.question: Kim's annual salary in year 1 is 16200 pounds and is predicted to be 31500 pounds in year 10. Model B assumes her salary increases by the same percentage each year. According to model B, find Kim's annual salary in year 2, to the nearest 10 pounds.
steps: Model B is geometric: 16200 r^9 = 31500, so r^9 = 35/18.

questions.question: Using model A and model B for Kim's salary (year 1 is 16200 pounds, year 10 is predicted 31500 pounds), calculate the difference between the total amounts she is predicted to earn from year 1 to year 10 inclusive. Give your answer to the nearest 10 pounds.
questions.answer: 7480 pounds (model A total 238500; model B total about 231019)
steps: Difference = 238500 - 231019.25 = 7480.75, which is 7480 to the nearest 10 pounds.

questions.question: A geometric sequence u_1, u_2, u_3, ... has common ratio r. Given that u_2 + u_3 = 6 and u_4 = 8, show that r satisfies 3r^2 - 4r - 4 = 0.

questions.topic: First Term From Sum To Infinity
questions.question: A geometric sequence has common ratio r satisfying 3r^2 - 4r - 4 = 0 and u_4 = 8. Given that the sequence has a sum to infinity, find u_1.
steps: A sum to infinity needs |r| < 1, so r = -2/3.

questions.question: A geometric sequence has first term u_1 = -27 and common ratio r = -2/3. Find the sum to infinity, S_infinity.
A geometric sequence has first term a and common ratio r. Given that S_infinity = 3a, show that r = 2/3.
steps: Divide by a (a is non-zero): 1/(1 - r) = 3.

questions.question: A geometric sequence has first term a and common ratio r = 2/3, with u^2 - u^4 = 16, where u^k is the kth term. Find the value of S_10, giving your answer to one decimal place.

The adult population of a town at the start of 2019 is 25000. A model predicts the adult population increases by 2% each year, so that the population at the start of each year forms a geometric sequence. According to the model, find the adult population of the town at the start of 2032.
steps: First term a = 25000 (start of 2019) and common ratio r = 1.02.
The start of 2032 is 13 years later, so the population is 25000 x 1.02^13.
So the population is about 32340 adults.

questions.question: Every member of the adult population gives 5 pounds to local charity at the start of each year. The adult population at the start of 2019 is 25000 and grows by 2% each year. Find the total amount of money given to charity by the adult population from 2019 to 2032 inclusive, giving your answer to the nearest 1000 pounds.
steps: Amount given in year k (k = 0 for 2019) = 5 x 25000 x 1.02^k, for k = 0 to 13 (14 years inclusive).
Total = 125000 x 15.97394 = 1996742, which is 1997000 to the nearest 1000 pounds.

questions.question: A geometric series has first term 20 and common ratio 7/8. Its sum to infinity is S_infinity. Find the value of S_infinity.
steps: |r| = 7/8 < 1, so the sum to infinity exists.

questions.question: The first term of a geometric series is 20 and the common ratio is 7/8. The sum to N terms is S_N. Find, to 1 decimal place, the value of S_12.
A geometric series has first term 20 and common ratio 7/8. The sum to infinity is S_infinity and the sum to N terms is S_N. Find the smallest value of N for which S_infinity - S_N < 0.5.
steps: Smallest integer N = 44 (check: N = 43 gives 0.513, N = 44 gives 0.449).

questions.question: The numbers of downloads of an app each month, in thousands, for the first three months after release are 2k - 15, k and k + 4, where k is a constant. The numbers are modelled as a geometric series. Show that k^2 - 7k - 60 = 0.
steps: For a geometric series, (second term)^2 = (first term)(third term).

questions.question: The numbers of downloads each month, in thousands, are 2k - 15, k and k + 4, modelled as a geometric series, with k^2 - 7k - 60 = 0. Predict the number of downloads in the 4th month.
steps: k = -5 gives month 1 downloads of -25 thousand, which is impossible, so k = 12.
The terms are 9, 12, 16, so the common ratio is r = 4/3.

questions.question: The monthly downloads (in thousands) form a geometric series 9, 12, 16, ... with common ratio 4/3. The total number of all downloads is predicted to exceed 3 million for the first time in the Nth month. Calculate the value of N according to the model.
questions.answer: N = 17 (the page prints no mark for part (c); the printed total of 6 equals (a) 2 + (b) 4)
steps: So N = 17 (check: S_16 = 2667 thousand, S_17 = 3565 thousand).

questions.question: A geometric series has first term a and common ratio r. Prove that the sum of the first n terms is S_n = a(1 - r^n)/(1 - r).
steps: Multiply by r: rS_n = ar + ar^2 + ... + ar^n.
Subtract: S_n - rS_n = a - ar^n, so S_n(1 - r) = a(1 - r^n).
Divide by (1 - r): S_n = a(1 - r^n)/(1 - r).

questions.question: A geometric series has second term -320 and fifth term 512/25. Find the value of the common ratio.
steps: Second term ar = -320 and fifth term ar^4 = 512/25.

questions.question: A geometric series has second term -320 and fifth term 512/25, so its common ratio is -2/5. Hence find the sum of the first 13 terms, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
steps: First term a: ar = -320 with r = -2/5, so a = -320/(-2/5) = 800.

questions.question: Owen runs every Sunday and every Wednesday over a 12-week training period. On Sunday in week 1 he runs 15 km and on Sunday in week 12 he runs 37 km. In plan A he increases his Sunday distance by the same amount each week. Calculate the distance he runs on Sunday in week 5 under plan A.

Owen's Sunday distances in plan B increase by the same percentage each week, from 15 km in week 1 to 37 km in week 12. Calculate the distance he runs on Sunday in week 5 under plan B, giving your answer in km to one decimal place.
steps: So the distance is 20.8 km to 1 dp.

questions.question: Owen also runs a fixed integer distance of x km every Wednesday over the 12 weeks. The total distance on Sundays and Wednesdays over the 12 weeks must not exceed 360 km. Find the maximum value of x (i) if he uses training plan A and (ii) if he uses training plan B. (Marks shown for part (c) as a whole: 5.)
steps: Wednesdays total 12x, so 312 + 12x <= 360, giving x <= 4. Maximum x = 4.
Plan B Sunday total: S_12 = 15(r^12 - 1)/(r - 1) with r = 1.085541, about 294.19 km.
294.19 + 12x <= 360 gives x <= 5.48, so the maximum integer x = 5.

questions.question: Adina saves 5 pounds in week 1, 5.25 pounds in week 2, 5.50 pounds in week 3, and so on until she has enough money to buy a computer. (i) State with a reason whether an arithmetic or a geometric series should be used. (ii) Write down an expression in n for the amount, in pounds, saved in week n. (Marks shown for part (a) as a whole: 3.)
questions.answer: (i) Arithmetic, because the weekly saving rises by the same 0.25 each week; (ii) u_n = 4.75 + 0.25n pounds.
steps: Weekly savings rise by 5.25 - 5 = 0.25 and 5.50 - 5.25 = 0.25, a constant difference, so use an arithmetic series.
First term a = 5 and common difference d = 0.25.
So the amount saved in week n is 4.75 + 0.25n pounds.

questions.question: Adina saves 5 pounds in week 1 and her savings increase by 0.25 pounds each week (5.25, 5.50, ...). The computer costs 350 pounds. Find the number of weeks it will take Adina to save enough money to buy the computer.
steps: n = (-39 + sqrt(12721))/2 = 36.89, so she needs more than 36 weeks.
S_36 = 337.5 (not enough) and S_37 = 351.5 (enough), so the answer is 37 weeks.

questions.question: A colony of bees has 30000 bees at the start of a study. Three years after the start of the study there are 34000 bees. A model predicts the number of bees increases by p% each year, so that the number at the end of each year forms a geometric sequence. Assuming the model, find the value of p, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.

A bee colony starts at 30000 and grows by p% each year (p = 4.26, from part (a)). According to the model, at the end of N years the number of bees exceeds 75000. Find, showing all steps, the smallest integer value of N.
steps: Number at the end of N years = 30000 r^N > 75000, so r^N > 2.5.
Take logs: N ln r > ln 2.5, where ln r = ln(17/15)/3 = 0.041721.

questions.question: A geometric sequence has first term 4 and common ratio 6. Given that the nth term is greater than 10^100, find the minimum possible value of n.
steps: So n - 1 >= 128, and the minimum n = 129.

questions.question: A geometric sequence has first term a and common ratio r. The second term of the sequence is -6 and the sum to infinity of the series is 25. Show that 25r^2 - 25r - 6 = 0.
steps: Sum to infinity a/(1 - r) = 25, so -6/(r(1 - r)) = 25.

questions.question: Write down the solutions of 25r^2 - 25r - 6 = 0.
Hence state the value of r, giving a reason for your answer, for the geometric sequence whose second term is -6 and whose sum to infinity is 25.
questions.answer: r = -1/5, because a sum to infinity exists only when |r| < 1.
steps: The sum to infinity exists only when |r| < 1.
r = 6/5 has |r| > 1, so it is rejected.

questions.question: For the geometric series with second term -6, sum to infinity 25 and common ratio r = -1/5, find the sum of the first 4 terms.
